statement: Place a decoupling capacitor, typically multilayer ceramic, 0.01–0.1 µF (rated >5 V), directly across the VCC-to-ground pins of each logic IC. Place it as close to the IC as possible so switching current spikes stay local instead of propagating into the supply line.
condition: Every digital/logic IC power pin pair in the design.

statement: As a coverage guideline, use at least one decoupling capacitor for every five to ten gates, or one for every five counter or register ICs.
condition: Boards with many small logic ICs where one capacitor per IC is impractical.

statement: Unused logic inputs that affect the chip's logical state must not float — tie them high or low as logic requires (unused NAND/AND inputs high, unused NOR/OR inputs low; flip-flop CLEAR/PRESET grounded or tied high as appropriate). Inputs of entirely unused sections of a CMOS IC should be grounded: floating unused-section inputs can charge to a level where output MOS transistors conduct simultaneously, causing excessive supply current and possible IC damage.
condition: Any logic IC with unused input pins or unused gates in a multi-gate package.

statement: A pull-up resistor holds an otherwise-floating input high; 10 kΩ is the typical value. Verify the resistor is small enough not to sag the input below the IC's minimum high threshold: Vin = Vsupply − R·IIH must stay above VIH,min (example: 74LS with IIH ≈ 20 µA and R = 10 kΩ gives Vin = 4.80 V at 5 V supply). Verify it is large enough that grounding the pin does not waste excessive power: PD = V²/R (10 kΩ at 5 V → 2.5 mW... 25 mW when switched).
condition: Logic/MCU input held high with a switch or open-drain driver pulling low.
formula: Vin = Vsupply - R*IIH ; PD = Vsupply^2 / R

statement: A pull-down resistor holds a floating terminal low and must be much smaller than a pull-up because the input low current IIL (sourced by the IC) is much larger than IIH — typically 100 Ω to 1 kΩ. Verify Vin = IIL·R stays below VIL,max (example: 74LS with IIL = 400 µA and 500 Ω gives 0.20 V, well under the ~0.8 V VIL,max). Beware power dissipation when the pin is driven high: PD = V²/R (500 Ω at 5 V → 50 mW).
condition: Logic/MCU input held low with a switch or push-pull driver pulling high.
